- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 1–2% above recent mean to avoid overreaction.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > 70), model tends to overcorrect; apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion to the forecast.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model often misreads trend direction; use 3-period moving average to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% above forecast, adjust future forecasts upward by 1–2% to account for mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent drop (last 3 days < 0.4), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect subdued market sentiment.
